brief: Midterm elections gave Democrats both chambers of Congress while Trump keeps the presidency and veto, which UBS reads as making abrupt tax and spending changes harder; the S&P 500 rose 1.6% and the Nasdaq 1.4% Wednesday, Treasury yields fell 8bps, and the dollar weakened (DXY -0.3%), reversing an initial negative futures reaction. UBS notes the S&P gained an average 15.5% in the six months after each of the 14 midterms since 1970, explicitly not a forecast. Within tech, large platforms rallied while data-center-linked names fell on fears that Democratic gains in states like Texas and Georgia bring tighter scrutiny of power, water and permitting, so UBS recommends rebalancing concentrated AI exposure toward financially strong, self-funded platforms. Separately, Qatar-mediated US-Iran talks and Trump's comment that no strike is imminent pushed Brent down 8.2% to about $93.8/bbl, though low inventories and exhausted SPR releases could keep oil elevated if diplomacy stalls. Firmer Eurozone inflation (4.0% y/y) reinforces a December ECB hike bet and further dollar weakness; UBS still expects EURUSD toward 1.16 by year-end. China's $70bn NVIDIA chip order data, with only 1% near-term fulfillment, is cited as evidence AI demand remains intact despite monetization-risk concerns; UBS forecasts AI capex at $1.0tr/$1.4tr/$1.5tr for 2026-2028.
